title: Debug: Every Employee "Shares" Their Own Salary
description:
This is meant to report employees who share their exact salary with **someone else** — but it currently returns literally every employee, even ones whose salary is completely unique in the company. Find the bug and fix it.

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
hint: Without excluding the row itself, every employee's salary trivially "matches" e2 = themselves — a correlated subquery comparing a table to itself almost always needs an explicit `e2.id <> e.id` (or similar) to rule out the row matching its own reflection.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);

tests.name: Department with no employees
Employees with NULL department and NULL salary
Single employee, single department
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','Engineer',100000,1,NULL,'2022-04-01');

tests.name: Duplicate names and same hire dates
Zero and negative salaries, boundary dates
All salaries unique — buggy query returns everyone, correct returns none
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'E','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ava','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Ben','E',90000,1,1,'2020-01-01'),(3,'Cara','E',80000,1,1,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: All salaries identical — everyone shares with others
Single employee — buggy returns them, correct returns none
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'E','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Two employees with same salary
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'E','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'A','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'B','E',100000,1,1,'2020-01-01');
